items.headline: Optimizely Web abused to inject malware into 178 organisations' sites
items.summary: Attackers injected malicious JavaScript into Optimizely Web customer projects on 16 November 2026, reaching visitors of 178 organisations including Zoom, BBC and CNN. Optimizely says the flaw is fixed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Optimizely acknowledged the incident; Report URI published independent analysis of 188 infected snippets.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026, first injection seen 04:21 UTC per Report URI (reported via Infosecurity Magazine)

sections.happened: On 16 November 2026, an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability in Optimizely Experimentation and injected malicious JavaScript into customer Project JavaScript fields. Report URI found it in 188 snippets across 178 organisations, including Zoom, the BBC and CNN. Optimizely says it has remediated the flaw.
sections.technical: Injected code runs on every page from Optimizely's CDN. It monitors pages for crypto wallet addresses to swap, skims card form fields, steals cookies and screenshots, and on iPhone and iPad loads Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits. No CVE or ATT&CK mapping published.
sections.guidance: Per Report URI: check Project JavaScript for 1688360.cc and atob(; update iOS to 18.7.3 or later, or 26.3 or later; deploy a Content Security Policy.
sections.differing: Crypto losses reported as $7,040 (Infosecurity Magazine), $7,150 (Help Net Security), about $7,000 (The Register). Clean-up time given as 23:11 UTC (Infosecurity) and 11:11 p.m. UTC (Search Engine Journal).
sections.unknown: How attackers gained access to customer projects, attacker identity, true victim count (likely higher), and card-skimming volume.

items.headline: Russian Cold Relic (Star Blizzard) uses cloud identity abuse to pivot between two US organisations
items.summary: Google GTIG and Mandiant report Russian group Cold Relic (Star Blizzard) chained two US cloud intrusions: super admin MFA-fatigue compromise, then Entra ID SSO phishing to reach a second organisation.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Google GTIG/Mandiant analysis; victims unnamed; primary blog not directly read.
items.firstReported: Google blog dated 17 Nov 2026 (time not stated); first press coverage Infosecurity Magazine, 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant published a 17 November 2026 analysis of Russian group Cold Relic (Star Blizzard). It describes two US intrusions: a late-2025 Google Workspace super admin compromise, then a 2026 Entra ID SSO-based breach at a second organisation. Google says the group remains active, with phishing observed in November 2026. Victims are unnamed.
sections.technical: Initial access: stolen super admin credentials plus MFA push fatigue, via a US residential proxy near the victim (late 2025). Persistence: rogue MFA devices, passkeys, backup codes. Exfiltration: bulk cloud drive download, employee lists, Workspace Takeout. Second intrusion: phishing links harvested Entra ID credentials and tokens. No CVEs reported.
sections.guidance: Google recommends phishing-resistant MFA, restricting and auditing passkey registrations, enriching logs with proxy/VPN reputation feeds, cloud DLP policies, and revoking all sessions when an intrusion is identified.
sections.differing: Vendor and secondary write-ups differ in detail: Aviatrix cites UNC4057 and audit-log exfiltration, which the GTIG text excerpts do not show. Google's account is treated as primary.
sections.unknown: Victims unnamed; total data volume unknown; full GTIG blog not directly readable, so excerpts were used.

items.headline: Suspected Chinese APT rebuilds EggStreme malware after exposure, still targeting Philippine government
items.summary: Bitdefender says a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt its EggStreme malware after public exposure and still targets multiple Philippine government organisations. New builds use a new protocol, passive backdoors and no keylogger.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Single vendor research update; victims unnamed; no attribution change.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (time not stated); Bitdefender blog, same day as The Hacker News and Infosecurity Magazine coverage

sections.happened: Bitdefender published an 18 November 2026 update to its September 2025 EggStreme research. It says a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt parts of the framework after exposure, with its report a likely trigger. It assesses with high confidence that multiple Philippine government organisations are targeted; Taiwan is a low-to-medium-confidence lead. No new attribution.
sections.technical: DLL sideloading under system library names, file-share staging over SMB with valid credentials, in-memory execution, mutual TLS. Agent moved to raw TCP with mutual TLS; some builds are passive listeners; newer builds lack the keylogger. Loader cipher changed from RC4 to RC5 to a custom cipher. Initial access unknown.
sections.guidance: Bitdefender recommends restricting unneeded built-in Windows tools, detecting DLL sideloading by library name and location, finding unmanaged machines that reach workstations, and watching for new inbound listeners on workstations.
sections.differing: Palo Alto Networks tracks CL-STA-1048, which used EggStremeFuel and EggStremeLoader from March to September 2025. Bitdefender says it has not compared infrastructure or victims to test whether these are one cluster.
sections.unknown: Initial access vector; victim identities and count; whether EggStremeWizard is still deployed; whether campaign-specific certificate authorities are confirmed; Taiwan targeting.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities discloses possible leak of customer data from test environment
items.summary: Japanese online broker Rakuten Securities says production customer data in a test environment may have leaked; up to 15.72M accounts potentially involved.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company's own 17 Nov disclosure; leak described as possible, not confirmed.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated in sources); company detected possible access 16 Nov, Infosecurity Magazine and Japan Times reported same period

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities detected possible unauthorised access to part of its systems on 16 Nov and blocked it. Its 17 Nov notice says test-environment information may have left the company on 11 Nov. Up to about 4.47M accounts had personal and financial details exposed; about 11.25M had branch codes and login IDs. Passwords and PINs were not reported exposed.
sections.technical: Company has not disclosed the attacker, entry method or cause; investigation ongoing. Production customer data was in a test environment, which usually holds dummy data, because of an internal system update. Mallory aggregator says an undisclosed vulnerability was exploited; not corroborated by the company.
sections.guidance: Company urges customers to switch to FIDO2 passkeys (over 90% of daily users already use them), warns of phishing, and says its emails contain no links. Customers can temporarily freeze trading and withdrawals in security settings.
sections.differing: Japan Times and Reuters-based reports give a 15.72M total; the company gives two separate tiers with no overlap per a spokesperson. Aggregators say the total double-counts overlapping accounts.
sections.unknown: Attacker, entry method, root cause and whether data was exfiltrated are unconfirmed. No regulator statement reported. Final affected count may change.

items.headline: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after account compromise affecting ~265,000 customers
items.summary: Transport for London took its photocard website offline after attackers compromised customer accounts, potentially affecting around 265,000 people. The ICO has been notified.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: TfL confirmed the incident via press statements; technical details thin.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, 11:01 UK (The Register); TfL says it first became aware 16 Nov 2026

sections.happened: On 16 November 2026, Oyster photocard customers received emails from TfL systems asking them to create accounts they already held. TfL says the emails resulted from the compromise. It took the photocard website down and says the incident is contained. Around 265,000 customers may have had account details compromised. TfL has notified the ICO and contacted affected customers. The website had no restoration date.
sections.technical: Entry route not disclosed. No CVE, ATT&CK mapping, malware or IOCs published. Attackers used TfL's own email systems to send account-creation messages to customers.
sections.guidance: TfL says all photocard customers will be asked to change passwords, security questions and answers, and advises changing reused passwords on other services. Customers should verify messages via TfL's official website or customer services.
sections.differing: TfL says no passwords, payment details or journey history were accessed. Infosecurity quotes CyberSmart's comment on phishing risk; this is third-party commentary, not an official finding.
sections.unknown: Entry method, attacker identity, exact data fields accessed, and when the website will return remain unconfirmed.

items.headline: Wellington IT attack exposes payee data at around 40 Irish credit unions
items.summary: Attack on Belfast IT supplier Wellington IT exposed saved payee details (names, IBANs, BICs, sort codes) of members at about 40 Irish credit unions. Passwords and funds reportedly unaffected.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Vendor, affected credit unions and minister confirm incident; technical cause unverified.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (Tuesday, per The Register; UK time not stated). BleepingComputer 18 Nov 2026, 14:39.

sections.happened: Attackers exploited an online banking platform weakness between 2 and 4 October 2026; the flaw was closed on 6 October. Wellington IT, owned by Vencora, notified credit unions only in mid-November. Minister Robert Troy called the delay not acceptable.
sections.technical: Reported as an automated script making five million requests against an authorisation flaw, using valid credentials. The Register reports a platform vulnerability. No CVE, ATT&CK mapping or IOCs published. Logs insufficient to confirm which records were accessed.
sections.guidance: Members advised to remain vigilant for phishing and impersonation. St Canice's warned members not to transfer money in response to anyone claiming funds must be moved for safety.
sections.differing: The Register describes a platform vulnerability; notices cited by BleepingComputer describe valid-credential abuse. Counts: about 40 Irish (Register, minister); 50 total, 43 Irish (BleepingComputer).
sections.unknown: Total individuals affected is unknown. Attacker and vector unattributed. Investigation ongoing with DPC, NCSC and Garda GNCCB.

items.summary: Ethiopian Airlines warned ShebaMiles loyalty members on 18 November 2026 that a limited-scope cyber incident may have exposed some customer information. No financial data evidence found; scale unknown.

items.labelBasis: Airline notice confirmed via multiple outlets; scope, date and data types undisclosed.
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026, Wednesday (UK time not stated); first seen via TechCabal and ShebaMiles member email

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 Ethiopian Airlines emailed ShebaMiles frequent-flyer members a 'Data Breach Public Notice' describing a cybersecurity incident of 'limited scope' that may have exposed some customer information. items.headline: Gentlemen ransomware group lists NVIDIA on leak site; NVIDIA investigates possible third-party incident
items.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group listed NVIDIA on its leak site with a countdown to 28 November and no proof. NVIDIA says it found no indication its own systems were affected and is investigating an incident that may have involved a third-party partner.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Rests on a ransomware group's leak-site listing that shows no samples. NVIDIA's statement acknowledges an investigation of a possible third-party incident but denies finding any NVIDIA system impact. No independent verification has been published.

sections.happened: The Gentlemen ransomware group added NVIDIA to its dark-web data leak site on 18 November 2026, according to trackers and researcher Dominic Alvieri's post on X as relayed by secondary outlets. The listing carries a countdown of about 234 hours ending on 28 November and threatens to publish data. BleepingComputer and iThome reported on 19 November that the listing includes no stolen files, no intrusion date and no description of the data. An NVIDIA spokesperson told BleepingComputer the company is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner and has found no indication that NVIDIA systems or networks were affected.
sections.technical: No technical details of an intrusion have been published. iThome reported that the listing gives a brief company description, Tox contact details for negotiation and the countdown, and does not state the data type or time of access. Secondary reports describe the data field as marked "SOON". The Gentlemen operates double extortion (exfiltration then encryption) and, per BleepingComputer, moved from a closed group to a RaaS model offering affiliates up to 90% of ransom proceeds. BleepingComputer says it has claimed more than 1,100 victims. No CVEs, ATT&CK techniques or IOCs were published for this claim.
sections.guidance: NVIDIA's published position, via a spokesperson to BleepingComputer: it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner, has found no indication that NVIDIA systems or networks were affected, and continues to monitor the situation. No advisory has been published.
sections.differing: The Gentlemen's listing implies it holds NVIDIA data but offers no proof. NVIDIA says it found no sign its own systems were compromised. Gadget Review and Digit report trackers list the claim as pending validation. Cybernews researcher Aras Nazarovas, quoted by Sportskeeda, said the group has a history of inflated claims. The claim is better described as unverified.
sections.unknown: Whether any data was stolen, and from whom, is unknown. Whether the partner incident NVIDIA mentions is the one behind the listing is unconfirmed. It is also unknown whether data will be published when the countdown ends.

items.headline: Microsoft agent-framework 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI carried a credential stealer; versions pulled, root cause unconfirmed
items.summary: Two PyPI releases of Microsoft's agent-framework (about 190,000 downloads a month), uploaded 17 November, ran a stealer at every Python start targeting Azure, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions credentials. Both were removed within minutes; how the attacker got publishing access is unconfirmed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: A Microsoft member commented on the project's GitHub issue that the compromised versions were pulled and an investigation is under way, and a Microsoft spokesperson spoke to The Register about repositories made private. Multiple firms (Wiz, StepSecurity, OX, SafeDep, Upwind) independently analysed the wheels. Root cause is not confirmed.

sections.happened: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package, the meta-package for its open-source AI agent toolkit (about 190,000 downloads a month), carried a credential stealer. Per StepSecurity, 1.26.1 was uploaded at 20:35 UTC (same as UK time) on 17 November and quarantined at 21:06; 1.26.2 was uploaded at 21:08, after that quarantine, and quarantined at 21:16. The last clean release is 1.26.0 (12 November). A Microsoft member wrote on GitHub that the versions were pulled and an investigation is under way. Wiz found 17 of 50 retained exfiltration requests came from three distinct victims. Microsoft told The Register it made some repositories private while investigating malicious content; the agent-framework repository was offline.
sections.technical: The wheels add .pth startup hooks (agent_framework_meta.pth in 1.26.1; af_runtime_diag.pth and .py in 1.26.2) that run at every Python start without importing the package; the genuine agent-framework-core 1.26.0 dependency kept the framework working. A detached child collects environment variables, up to 60 (80 in 1.26.2) credential files (Azure CLI, .npmrc, .netrc, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, .env), and /proc/*/environ of up to 300 processes. It requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps OIDC and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, then sends one zlib/base64 POST to a webhook.site URL. Researchers found no second stage. No CVE assigned. ATT&CK mapping (not vendor-published): T1195.002, T1546.018, T1552, T1528, T1567. Actor unattributed.
sections.guidance: The Microsoft member said the versions were pulled from the feed. Upwind's issue states 1.26.0 is clean, copies persist in pip/uv caches, CI caches and mirrors, and credential revocation was unconfirmed. StepSecurity advises isolating affected hosts, rebuilding from a clean base, pinning 1.26.0 and reviewing OIDC and managed-identity permissions.
sections.differing: Root cause is disputed. Wiz says the attacker appears to have compromised a client certificate and key for Microsoft's ESRP release pipeline, publishing from Microsoft-owned IP space after an AWS attempt failed. Upwind says a PyPI upload credential outside Microsoft's control, with hand-repacked wheels. SafeDep flags same-day maintainer account vibiret, unconfirmed. Microsoft has not confirmed any.
sections.unknown: How the attacker obtained publishing access, who uploaded the files, whether the credential is revoked, total installs and victim count, and the reason for offline Microsoft repositories remain unconfirmed.

items.headline: Apache Roller RCE flaw CVE-2026-129448 actively exploited
items.summary: Apache says CVE-2026-129448, an unauthenticated deserialization flaw in Roller's XML-RPC endpoint (CVSS 9.8), is being actively exploited. Fixed in 6.1.6.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Apache advisory quoted by three outlets; primary advisory not opened.
items.firstReported: Apache advisory dated 17 Nov 2026 (time not stated); first press report BleepingComputer, 18 Nov 2026, 05:35 AM stamp (zone not stated)

sections.happened: The Apache Software Foundation said in a 17 November 2026 advisory that CVE-2026-129448 in Apache Roller is being actively exploited, allowing unauthenticated code execution. Apache has not said who is attacking or how many servers are compromised.
sections.technical: Unsafe deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint (/roller-services/xmlrpc): vendor extension types are deserialized before the requester is authenticated. CVSS 9.8. Affects 4.0.0 through 6.1.4; fixed in 6.1.6. Same flaw as CVE-2026-82384, patched September 2026. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI does not block it.
sections.guidance: Upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later. If upgrading is not possible, set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, and restart Roller.
sections.differing: Outlets agree on the facts. BleepingComputer gives the advisory as Tuesday; SecurityWeek and The Hacker News give 17 November, which is the same day.
sections.unknown: Attackers, targets, attack method, number of compromised servers and published IOCs are not given by Apache in the sources reviewed.

items.headline: Five critical NGINX 'NGINX2Root' flaws disclosed with public PoC exploits
items.summary: Researchers disclosed five critical NGINX flaws (CVSS 4.0 9.2) enabling unauthenticated remote code execution under ASLR bypass conditions. F5 fixed them in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. Public PoCs exist.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: F5 acknowledged and patched; multiple outlets report the same CVEs
items.firstReported: 18 November 2026, UK time; first source: Infosecurity Magazine (researcher disclosures by Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, Xint)

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026, researchers at Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7 and Xint disclosed five critical NGINX flaws, branded NGINX2Root, rated 9.2 on CVSS 4.0. F5 fixed them in NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 and NGINX Plus 37.0.8.1 and 37.3.0.1. Public proof-of-concept exploits are available. No exploitation in the wild has been reported.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-123007: HTTP/2 integer underflow leading to heap overflow (CWE-191), affecting versions since 1.9.5. CVE-2026-123633: HTTP/2 use-after-free. CVE-2026-121810: HTTP/3 use-after-free. CVE-2026-123634: resolver, proxy_pass and mirror setup. CVE-2026-113425: mail proxy. Code execution requires ASLR disabled or bypassed.
sections.guidance: F5 and CIRCL advise upgrading to 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 and fully restarting NGINX, not just reloading. CIRCL advises disabling HTTP/2 until patched. F5 lists workarounds only for CVE-2026-123634 and CVE-2026-113425.
sections.differing: Wiz says CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 can bypass ASLR; F5 says code execution requires ASLR disabled or bypassed. Disclosures differ on flaw count: Ikotas reports one, Wiz two, Xint five.
sections.unknown: Whether exploitation occurs in the wild. Ubuntu and Debian had no fixed packages at publication. Rapid7's exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic.

items.headline: CISA adds exploited Perforce Puppet Enterprise RCE CVE-2026-115731 to KEV
items.summary: CISA added Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS 9.4), a deserialization remote code execution bug in Puppet Server, to its KEV catalog. Federal fix deadline is 1 December 2026.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: CISA KEV listing; Perforce reports no known exploitation; no public attack details
items.firstReported: Date only (17 Nov 2026 KEV addition per Help Net Security; time not stated); Security Affairs article dated 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: Perforce released fixes for CVE-2026-115731 on 3 November 2026. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Tuesday 17 November and ordered federal civilian agencies to fix it by 1 December 2026. Perforce says it knows of no attacks and no customer data access.
sections.technical: Deserialization of untrusted data in Puppet Server report processing. A client holding a Puppet CA-signed certificate can send a crafted report via HTTP PUT for code execution as the Puppet Server service account. Autosigning allows unauthenticated certificate acquisition. Fixed in PE 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1, 2023.8.13; Puppet Core 9.1.3, 8.22.2.
sections.guidance: Perforce: upgrade to the fixed versions and restart the server as soon as possible. If unable, review autosign configuration and authorization rules as a temporary mitigation.
sections.differing: Perforce says it is not aware of attacks; Help Net Security says attackers are exploiting the flaw. Security Affairs reports no confirmed exploitation. The KEV listing indicates exploitation.
sections.unknown: Attack details, victims, threat actor and IOCs are unpublished. The CISA KEV entry and Perforce advisory were not retrieved directly.

items.headline: Java4Shell: critical OpenJDK Base64 flaw (CVE-2026-114938) patched; scanning and exploitation attempts reported
items.summary: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938, a heap overflow in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder, on 17 November after a leak; OpenJDK and Oracle shipped fixes the same day. Honeypot operators report probing and blind exploit attempts from 17-19 November, but no confirmed intrusion.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Oracle's CVE record and advisory, the OpenJDK advisory (cited by Calif, VulnCheck and GreyNoise), CISA's alert (via The Hacker News and The Record) and Canada's Cyber Centre alert acknowledge the flaw and fixes. VulnCheck independently reproduced the overflow. Exploitation attempts rest on GreyNoise, watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian telemetry; successful compromise is unconfirmed.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026, before 16:59 UK time (The Hacker News reported the leak); fixes released 21:00 UK time, Calif write-up about 21:13

sections.happened: Calif, a California security firm, disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) on 17 November 2026, after details leaked ahead of coordinated disclosure. OpenJDK and Oracle released fixes at 21:00 UK time; GreyNoise's timeline puts Calif's write-up at 21:13 and Oracle's CVE record shows publication at 21:32. CISA and Canada's Cyber Centre issued alerts that evening. Cisco, Siemens, Elastic, Red Hat, Atlassian and Keycloak have since published impact notices, while Amazon, Microsoft and Azul released patched builds (SecurityWeek). By early 19 November GreyNoise had logged 150+ matching requests from five IPs; watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian also report probing. None has confirmed a successful intrusion.
sections.technical: Root cause: an integer underflow in HotSpot's x86-64 AVX-512 VBMI Base64 decode intrinsic (CWE-122). Input of 64 'A' plus '=' (128 on JDK 17) makes a 64-byte store land 62 bytes past a 50-byte buffer. Affected: OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later (17, 21, 25, 27) and downstream builds, only on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI; ARM is unaffected. Oracle scores CVSS 3.1 8.1 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N); Calif scores CVSS 4.0 9.2. Calif demonstrated pre-auth RCE in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, and authenticated RCE in Kafka, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker, using bespoke heap grooming. No actor attributed; no ATT&CK IDs or malware published.
sections.guidance: Oracle's fixed builds per Canada's Cyber Centre: 8u513-perf, 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1. Calif, Red Hat and VulnCheck list the workarounds -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or -XX:UseAVX=2. Atlassian suggests disabling AVX-512 for Data Center; Cisco has no workaround; Siemens suggests taking Industrial Edge instances offline; Keycloak published 26.8.2-3.
sections.differing: Severity: Oracle rates it 8.1 (High, AC:H); Calif 9.2 and Red Hat Critical. Exploitability: Calif reports default-configuration RCE; VulnCheck found a crash trivial but RCE needing heap grooming and an application-specific leak, yet says its own RCE exploit exists. Pre-disclosure Upwind and Equixly predicted only a crash, unreproduced. The RCE claims are better supported: vendor-confirmed impact, VulnCheck's exploit.
sections.unknown: Whether any probing has compromised a system is unconfirmed. Calif's product-specific chains remain unpublished, timing unknown. Cisco IOS XE and UCS Central status, remaining vendor patches and exposed-host numbers are unreported.

items.headline: PHP schedules critical security release for 19 November, including RCE flaw CVE-2026-115560
items.summary: The PHP security team said releases for all supported versions would ship 19 November, 14:00-14:30 UTC, with highest severity Critical but needing non-default setups. CVE-2026-115560, a session-handling RCE, is expected in it. Fixed versions and details were unpublished at last check.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Rests on the PHP project's own 18 November notice and 23 October informational advisory on php.net, both read, plus consistent reporting by The Register, The Hacker News and SecurityWeek. Fixed versions and the full CVE list were not yet published at last check.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (PHP notice on php.net, time not stated); The Register published 22:38 UTC (22:38 UK time)

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 the PHP security team posted a notice on php.net that security releases would be published on Thursday 19 November between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC (the same as UK time on that date). It said they are part of the regular four-week cycle, affect all supported PHP versions, and carry a highest severity of Critical. Issues rated Critical need non-default configuration or uncommon setups. Technical details and fixed version numbers are to be published with the releases. The notice follows the 21 October PHP2Shell emergency fixes (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619). At the time of research (about 14:10 UTC on 19 November) php.net's news archive still showed only the advance notice.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-115560 is a remote code execution vector in session upload progress, disclosed in a 23 October informational advisory. Preconditions: the application sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in configuration, switches it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and session.upload_progress.enabled is still on. PHP has not published CVSS, affected versions or root cause; sources say it is not fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. The notice does not say which flaws are rated Critical, so linking that rating to this CVE is the outlets' inference. No exploitation of CVE-2026-115560 reported. PHP2Shell (CVSS 9.2 each, per CERT-EU) was added to CISA's KEV catalogue on 26 October per The Register.
sections.guidance: PHP's notice says users are strongly encouraged to prepare to upgrade promptly once releases are available; fixed versions will be published with them. Its 23 October advisory suggests session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release; nothing further for those who already applied it for CVE-2026-109619. The Hacker News adds PHP workers must be restarted.
sections.differing: No dispute found. PHP says the 23 October RCE needs a very unlikely configuration and code combination (executive director Elizabeth Barron to The Register), so it was handled in the regular cycle. The Hacker News and SecurityWeek link CVE-2026-115560 to the Critical rating; PHP's notice does not name which issue is Critical.
sections.unknown: Fixed version numbers, the full CVE list, CVSS scores and which issue is rated Critical are unpublished. Whether other flaws in the release are exploitable by default, and whether exploitation will follow, is unknown.

items.headline: Ukraine and FBI arrest four suspected members of ransomware group tied to $40.5M in ransoms
items.summary: Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, detained four key suspects of a ransomware group linked to at least 28 companies paying over $40.5M in ransoms.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Ukrainian police and Prosecutor General announced arrests; ransom figures are police statements.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, 6:08 PM UK time (BleepingComputer); Prosecutor General's Office announcement reported by The Record on Wednesday 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: Ukrainian police and the Prosecutor General's Office, working with the FBI, ran 66 searches in Kyiv and 11 regions and detained four suspected key members of a ransomware group of at least 27 people. Police say at least 28 companies paid over $40.5M. Suspects face charges carrying up to 15 years.
sections.technical: Attackers posed as IT support by phone, using an AI-generated voice platform to obtain credentials or get remote-access tools installed. Court records describe a fake corporate VPN login page and a relayed 2FA code. Data was stolen, files encrypted, and victims extorted. Court records name Chaos ransomware; police did not.
sections.differing: Court records, reported by LeMagIT, say BlackSuit claimed Maxxis in 2024; police have not tied suspects to BlackSuit or confirmed Conti membership individually.
sections.unknown: Full damages, ransomware strain confirmation, identities of the suspects, and whether further arrests follow remain unconfirmed.

items.headline: US rule curbs Chinese remote access to AI chips in overseas data centres; Tencent, Beijing and Nvidia respond
items.summary: The US Commerce Department's BIS issued an interim final rule on 16 November requiring licences for AI chips going to data centres serving China-headquartered firms, and to five more countries. Tencent says it sets Chinese firms back; Beijing condemned it.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: The US Bureau of Industry and Security published the interim final rule and a press release, and the rule text was read directly. Tencent, Singapore's ministries and China's foreign ministry on-record responses are reported or published.

sections.happened: On 16 November 2026 the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule, "Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors" (RIN 0694-AK50). BIS said it was "written by and at the direction of" the Treasury Department and National Security Council. It requires licences for advanced AI chips destined for data centres, anywhere, that supply large compute to China-headquartered companies. It also adds a licence requirement for five countries and formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule. It takes effect on Federal Register publication, scheduled for 19 November. Tencent's president said it "sets everyone back in China". Al Jazeera reported Nvidia shares fell 4.1% on 17 November.
sections.technical: BIS rule text: new §744.24 requires a licence where an exporter knows items are going to a data centre that gives companies headquartered in China, Macau or other D:5 countries access to more than 12,000,000 aggregate TPP, at one site or "linked" sites. Commercial recommender systems are excluded. Existing providers must obtain a licence within 90 days of the effective date. Licences are also required for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, case by case, with an exemption for US-headquartered recipients who report. BIS says §744.23(a)(3) always covered transactions made "on behalf of" such firms, for example where they use over 50% of capacity. Comments are due 60 days after publication. CSIS puts the threshold at roughly 750 H200 GPUs.
sections.guidance: BIS states that entities in violation of the existing §744.23(a)(3) requirement "should submit a voluntary self-disclosure". It also says exporters should obtain data-centre know-your-customer information, treating refusal as a red flag. Commerce says it will monitor countries that tolerate evasion. Singapore's ministries say they are engaging affected companies and US authorities, and exploring trusted access for Singapore firms.
sections.differing: China's foreign ministry (state position) called the rule "economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction". BIS says it closes circumvention via third-country data centres. Tom's Hardware and The Hill reported a 90-day delay to taking effect; the rule text and law-firm analyses say effective on publication, with 90 days only for existing providers.
sections.unknown: Federal Register publication was not confirmed here. The 12,000,000 TPP measurement basis is unclear. Enforcement scope is open. Whether China retaliates is unknown; presidents Trump and Xi are due to meet in Shenzhen on 19 November.

items.headline: Scattered Spider member Tyler Buchanan sentenced to six years in US federal prison
items.summary: A Scottish national linked to Scattered Spider received 72 months for SMS phishing and SIM-swap thefts of at least $11.6M in cryptocurrency from US individuals. Restitution hearing set for 11 December.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: US DOJ press release (primary) with sentence, plea and co-defendant details.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (US time, Tuesday) via US Attorney's Office, Central District of California press release; reported 18 Nov

sections.happened: Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, was sentenced to 72 months by Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana, California, on 17 November 2026. He pleaded guilty on 17 April to wire fraud conspiracy and aggravated identity theft. He is the fifth and final defendant sentenced.
sections.technical: Between September 2021 and April 2023, the group sent hundreds of smishing texts impersonating employers or IT/BPO suppliers to employees at at least a dozen companies. A phishing kit relayed credentials to a Telegram channel. SIM swaps bypassed SMS two-factor authentication to drain individual crypto wallets.
sections.differing: Securityaffairs and Malwarebytes give the Spanish arrest in Palma de Mallorca as May 2024; MLQ says June 2024. The DOJ release gives no arrest date. Plea-stage proceeds were $8M; the DOJ figure is $11.6M.
sections.unknown: Restitution amount is undetermined until the 11 December hearing. Cryptocurrencies stolen have not been identified publicly.

items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold first trilateral summit in Shenzhen; four-point 'peace declaration' published
items.summary: The US, Chinese and Russian presidents met for roughly 80 minutes in Shenzhen on 19 November. Xinhua published a four-point declaration on UN reform, refined-fuel supply, ICC jurisdiction and nuclear-risk dialogue; it does not mention Ukraine or Iran.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Meeting and declaration text are reported by multiple outlets (Al Jazeera, AFP via Korea Herald, Semafor, Kyiv Post, Euronews) with agency pool photographs, and the Kremlin spokesperson commented. The declaration text was published by Chinese state media (Xinhua); no US or Russian government release of the text was found.

sections.happened: Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held what outlets describe as their first three-way meeting on 19 November 2026 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Xi chaired. Semafor and Euronews put the length at about 80 minutes; CCTV, cited by CNN, said about an hour and a half. Trump said the three countries hold the largest nuclear arsenals and that they were "making history". Xi called for shedding a "Cold War mentality". Xinhua published the declaration at 18:58 Beijing time (10:58 UK). Euronews reported Trump and Putin left Shenzhen soon after. Reuters, per a secondary summary, reported no closing statements by the leaders.
sections.technical: Xinhua's text, titled "China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace", has four points. (1) The three UN Security Council permanent members commit to reform the UN. (2) They plan to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products and reaffirm stable energy flows. (3) State consent and immunities of state officials are "of paramount importance"; the ICC and similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. (4) A nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought; the three will hold a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. No dates, mechanisms or figures are given. Kyiv Post notes no mention of Ukraine; Al Jazeera notes none of the Iran war.
sections.differing: Semafor calls the summit long on symbolism and short on substance. Peskov said Ukraine was not the "central topic"; Trump had said he asked Xi to help on Ukraine. Trump said Xi agreed Hormuz must stay open and Iran must not obtain nuclear weapons; that is reported only through Trump. Al Jazeera says the energy pledge's delivery is unclear.
sections.unknown: No US or Russian government release of the text was found; wording rests on Xinhua. Unclear: whether it is binding, when the nuclear dialogue starts, and whether Putin attends next month's Miami G20.

items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026, priced at $3 per million input and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1-million-token context window, for API, Gemini app and Antigravity users.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Google's own announcement and API release notes; multiple outlets report the same details.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (Google blog and Gemini API release notes); The Register, 19 Nov 2026 08:30 UTC

sections.happened: Google announced Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026, rolling it out in the Gemini API and AI Studio, Gemini for business, Antigravity for paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers. It sits between Hydrogen and Carbon in the Gemini 4 family. A cyber-focused variant is going to eligible Fairwind Program members.
sections.technical: Priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 cached) and $15 per million output, with a 1M-token context window. Four thinking levels; default is high. Google cites 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at xhigh and 58.6 on its Coding Agent Index. Model code gemini-4-neon.
sections.guidance: Per Google: Fairwind Program members should contact their Cloud account team to request access to the cyber variant. Google recommends testing thinking levels and choosing the lowest that meets quality needs.
sections.differing: Scores are Google's own claims or third-party indices it cites; independent verification is limited. Notebookcheck notes Neon is not available to free users. Unite.AI notes the 32% saving is per task at default thinking, not per token.
sections.unknown: Full Safety & Security Report was promised in coming days. Fairwind rollout timing and scope beyond eligible members are not detailed.

items.headline: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge rail section for third time in a week; Putin rules out partial ceasefires and vows retaliation
items.summary: Ukraine said Neptune missiles hit the Crimean Bridge's rail section overnight on 18–19 November, after strikes on 16 and 17 November collapsed a road span. Russia briefly halted trains. Putin later ruled out partial truces and promised a response.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Both Ukraine (General Staff, Defence Ministry) and Russia (Transport Ministry, Crimea's Moscow-installed head, Putin) acknowledge the strikes and the suspension of rail traffic; reported by multiple outlets. Damage extent is contested.
items.firstReported: Overnight 18–19 Nov 2026 (Aksyonov confirmed just after midnight local time; Kyiv Independent published 00:04 GMT on 19 Nov)

sections.happened: Ukraine struck the 19 km Kerch (Crimean) Bridge overnight on 18–19 November, the third attack in a week after strikes on 16 and 17 November. The 17 November strike destroyed a metal arch and road span; road traffic has been impossible since. Ukraine's Defence Ministry said Neptune missiles hit near the arch and on the rail tracks, halting trains. Russia's Transport Ministry said no one was hurt and rail services were temporarily suspended. Crimea's Moscow-installed head, Sergei Aksyonov, said rail would resume around 16:00 local time (13:00 GMT). Speaking after a Shenzhen summit with Trump and Xi, Putin said Russia would not negotiate partial ceasefires and that its response would be "far more painful".
sections.technical: Kinetic strike, not a cyber incident. Ukraine's General Staff attributed the 19 November attack to Ukrainian Navy Neptune coastal-defence missiles. For 17 November, Zelensky said Palianytsia drones hit the road section, while Neptune missiles, Ruta and FP-5 (Flamingo) weapons hit the rail section, as the seventh phase of a multi-week operation that first targeted air defences, radars and electronic-warfare assets. Ukraine's SBU said it destroyed one arch and the road span beneath it. Ukraine stated the weapons were domestically produced. Russia's Investigative Committee opened a terrorism case on 17 November. No ATT&CK, CVE or IOC data apply.
sections.guidance: Russian officials published: Deputy PM Marat Khusnullin said a restoration plan with three options was agreed, timelines would be assessed within a week, and parts could reopen in one to two months. Crimea's government said free boats run from 20 November between Crimea and Port Kavkaz; fuel in canisters is not allowed aboard. Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt.
sections.differing: Ukraine's General Staff calls the bridge the main route for Russian fuel, ammunition and equipment. Putin says it has long not been used for military equipment, ammunition or fuel; Reuters notes Russian forces rely more on a land corridor. Krymsky Veter eyewitnesses said the rail arch looked undamaged; Putin said the rail section was already restored.
sections.unknown: Extent of rail damage, whether services have normalised, and the nature and timing of Russia's promised response remain unknown. Reconstruction estimates differ: one Ukrainian expert said a year or more; Russian officials cite one to two months for parts.

items.headline: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83 a share, raising $81.3bn; Nasdaq trading as ANT due 19 November
items.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above the $70–$78 range, selling 980 million shares for about $81.3bn, the largest listing on record. With a $26bn private placement the total is $107.3bn. Nasdaq trading as ANT is due today.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Anthropic's own pricing announcement (18 Nov) gives price, share count, listing venue and ticker; Reuters, CNBC, CNN, Bloomberg and others report the same figures and the $81.3bn proceeds. SEC 424(b)(4) prospectus could not be opened by the researcher.

sections.happened: Anthropic, PBC announced on 18 November that it priced its IPO of Class A common stock at $83.00 a share, above the $70–$78 range set when the roadshow launched on 10 November (825 million shares). The offering was upsized to 980 million shares: 956,351,354 sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders. At $83 that is about $81.3bn, which Reuters and CNN report as exceeding SpaceX's $75bn June IPO. A separate $26bn private placement brings the total to $107.3bn (Reuters, Bloomberg). Shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq under "ANT" on 19 November (US market open is 14:30 UK); closing is expected 20 November.
sections.technical: Figures from Anthropic's announcement and Reuters. The registration statement was declared effective by the SEC on 18 November. Underwriters hold a 30-day option on up to 147 million more shares. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead a 22-bank syndicate (Reuters). Reuters reports a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5tn and about $1.1tn undiluted. Calcalist reports the placement is non-voting shares sold to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. Reuters, citing the filing, reports $81bn annualised revenue run-rate at 31 October, Q3 revenue of $16.96bn, an operating loss of $567m, and nearly $900bn of compute commitments.
sections.guidance: Anthropic's announcement says the offering is made only by means of a prospectus, available from Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, and that closing is subject to customary conditions. It states it will not receive proceeds from the selling stockholders' shares.
sections.differing: Headline totals differ by basis: $81.3bn is the public offering including selling stockholders' shares; $107.3bn adds the $26bn private placement (Semafor leads with $107bn). Valuation is quoted as about $1.5tn fully diluted by Reuters and about $1.1tn non-diluted. Reuters notes Anthropic faces questions on growth and spending; Semafor cites US regulation and infrastructure-funding risks.
sections.unknown: The opening price and first-day performance were not known at time of writing. Bloomberg reported gray-market indications of a 22–26% rise, which are not trading results. The researcher could not open the SEC 424(b)(4) filing.
